source_acquisition.search_note: reports/tables/visual_source_inventory.csv 将该论文记录为 no_public_source_found，且 corpus/visual_sources/icml-2026-87a216e14f5b/ 不存在；随后以 PDF 首页/参考文献的 OpenReview、arXiv 和代码线索搜索 GitHub，完整标题命中作者 Wenxiang-Diao/Privacy-Aware-VAD。gh 递归树确认仓库包含 assets/figures 下的 10 个 PNG：Figure 1 的四个 UMAP、Figure 2 pipeline、Figure 3 三个超参数图和 Figure 4 两个图；它们与 PDF 的 pdfimages 提取按像素逐一相等。仓库没有 figure/plot/table 生成脚本、TeX/TikZ/PGF、notebook 或 Figure 5/6/Table 1–29 的源文件，因此只记为 partial_visual_source；没有下载数据集、权重或 checkpoint。

paper_style.palette_strategy: 图内 raster 主要沿用 Matplotlib 分类色：UMAP 用多类别颜色，折线/柱图用蓝红或 tab10 数据集色，Figure 6 用蓝—白—红发散色；OPL/G-OPL 的蓝/红语义在流程图中明确，但没有一套跨所有图表的统一色板。大多数颜色在灰度下不可安全区分，表格则以黑色文字、粗体/下划线承担主语义。
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: 正文、caption、表格文字和规则是 PDF vector objects；Figure 1–6 的主体均是嵌入 raster PNG（Figure 2 也是 PNG 流程图），没有可供本审计确认的图内矢量绘图源码。
paper_style.style_consistency: 会议版式和表格字体稳定使用 Nimbus Roman No9 L/Computer Modern math，表格采用少量横线的 partial-grid 结构；Matplotlib raster 图的 DejaVu Sans 风格、字号和图例密度与 TeX 正文存在明显断层，尤其在 Figure 3–5 的小字号图例和宽表中。

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1. UMAP (McInnes et al., 2018) of removed features on MSAD (Zhu et al., 2024). OPL removes nuisance factors, yielding dispersed clusters, while G-OPL suppresses facial cues, producing a compact, overlapping distribution not aligned with anomaly types. This contrast shows their complementary roles in separating nuisance and privacy-sensitive information.

color.semantic_mapping: Each panel maps scenario or anomaly-type categories to a distinct color; panel titles distinguish OPL from G-OPL and the two label partitions.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: inside the lower/side area of each panel

encodings.shape: cross marker for embedded scatter glyphs
encodings.text: panel titles and per-panel categorical legends

figures.data_and_statistics: UMAP coordinates of removed feature vectors from MSAD; roughly thousands of frame-level points are shown without axes, aggregation, error estimates, or repeated-run summaries. Color is categorical and the embedding has no metric units.
figures.evidence_relation: Abstract claim about complementary nuisance and privacy-sensitive subspaces → Figure 1 qualitative contrast → method definitions of OPL/G-OPL and the projection objective → Figure 5 feature-level separation → Tables 2–5 utility/privacy results. The caption makes the qualitative conclusion explicit but does not give the UMAP preprocessing or sample count.
design_strengths: Four panels put the same nuisance/privacy contrast on one visual plane.
Dense point clouds and categorical legends make the qualitative cluster-shape claim inspectable without inventing a quantitative axis.
The exact four PDF raster images match the four public repository assets.
design_weaknesses: No axes, scale, sampling rule, or UMAP random-state information is visible.
Twelve-item legends are very dense at single-column width and color is not grayscale-safe.
Scenario/anomaly color semantics change by panel, so a reader must repeatedly consult each legend.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a 2×2 qualitative embedding grid only when panel titles and local legends identify the label partition; pair it with a caption that states which component is removed and which component remains task-relevant.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2. Pipeline overview. The Orthogonal Projection Layer (OPL, light blue) and its guided variant (G-OPL, dark blue and red) are lightweight, fully differentiable, and easily integrate into standard anomaly detection architectures (black). OPL suppresses nuisance factors through orthogonal projections, while G-OPL explicitly removes sensitive attributes via semantic suppression (λface Lcos) guided by attribute signals (e.g., faces, red arrows). An orthogonality regularizer (λorth Lorth) ensures stable optimization. OPL / G-OPL can be flexibly inserted after a feature extractor (or encoder), individual layer, or block. This design embeds privacy directly into the model, enabling precise control over sensitive information at the representation level with minimal impact on detection performance. See Appendix H, I, and M for practical insights on layer placement and privacy protection.

color.semantic_mapping: Light/dark blue identify OPL/G-OPL, red marks face guidance, purple marks orthogonality loss, and black marks the host VAD architecture.

encodings.line: colored directed arrows for original, face, and orthogonality losses
encodings.text: Videos, RetinaFace/faces, extractor, blocks, OPL/G-OPL, classifier, and loss labels

figures.data_and_statistics: A conceptual data-flow diagram rather than a measured plot; it contains no units, aggregation, repetitions, uncertainty, or quantitative marks. The visual encodes insertion points and gradient/loss paths.
figures.evidence_relation: Method claim that OPL/G-OPL are plug-and-play → Figure 2 interface → Eqs. (1)–(8) and Algorithms 1–2 → placement ablation Figure 4 and Tables 10/20–29 → utility/privacy Tables 4–8. The caption independently defines the color roles and points to Appendix H/I/M.
design_strengths: Left-to-right flow exposes where the privacy module sits relative to encoder, blocks, and classifier.
Color and arrow semantics separate host architecture from the face and orthogonality training signals.
The caption names insertion flexibility and the loss terms needed to interpret the arrows.
design_weaknesses: The raster is narrow and text becomes small when reproduced; there is no legend or numbered callout system.
The diagram does not show tensor dimensions, temporal aggregation, or exactly how the residual enters the classifier.
Red/blue/purple semantics depend on color and are weakened in grayscale.
figures.reusable_pattern: Represent a plug-in representation module with one left-to-right host-model spine plus separately colored training-signal arrows; define every color in the caption when no legend is present.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3. Evaluation of key hyperparameters.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue/red and light/dark variants distinguish AUC/AP or backbone/dataset series across the three hyperparameter panels.

encodings.x: candidate k or λface/λorth values; treated as categorical candidate settings

figures.data_and_statistics: Sensitivity curves over candidate rank and loss weights. Panel (a) reports AUC/AP for k values; panels (b) and (c) report AUC for RTFM/MGFN and ShT/UCF settings. Points are single reported values with no error bars, bands, repetitions, or uncertainty intervals.
figures.evidence_relation: Hyperparameter-choice claim → Figure 3 sensitivity windows and non-monotonic rank behavior → Table 1 and Appendix Tables 10–12 → practical default settings and layer-placement Figure 4. The one-line caption leaves the exact metrics, candidate sets, and series mapping to the graphic/text.
design_strengths: Three aligned panels let the reader compare rank and two regularization weights in one ablation object.
Marker and line-style redundancy helps distinguish the paired series where color is crowded.
The source assets are exact public PNGs, preserving the visible candidate labels and grid.
design_weaknesses: The caption is not self-contained: it does not define x candidates, datasets, metrics, or direction arrows.
Small legends and dual metric/series encodings create a high reading burden in a single column.
No uncertainty or run variation is displayed, so local peaks may look more decisive than supported.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use small-multiple sensitivity panels with a common visual grammar, but state the candidate set, metric, backbone, and selection rule in the caption or adjacent text.

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: Figure 4. (a) Ablation on OPL/G-OPL placement across datasets with RTFM. GmOn: m G-OPL and n OPL layers. (b) We select model with more G-OPL layers that achieves reasonable VAD performance for privacy decay (PD) curve.

color.semantic_mapping: Bars in (a) map to ShanghaiTech, UCF, CUHK, and Ped2; bars in (b) map to dataset-specific PD curves.

encodings.x: GmOn placement configurations in (a), first/second probe positions in (b)

figures.data_and_statistics: Grouped categorical bars compare OPL/G-OPL layer placement across four datasets; the small right panel shows the privacy-decay probe values for the selected multi-G-OPL model. Values are point estimates with no uncertainty display.
figures.evidence_relation: Layer-placement hypothesis → Figure 4(a) configuration comparison → Appendix Tables 20–29 exhaustive placement slices → Figure 4(b), Tables 6 and 9 privacy decay/efficiency → default one-early-G-OPL recommendation. The caption defines GmOn but not the bar order or probe sample size.
design_strengths: The two panels connect utility placement and privacy decay rather than treating them as unrelated results.
Dataset color is consistent within the placement panel and a horizontal grid supports approximate AUC reading.
The exact public assets allow the placement labels and compact PD panel to be reused.
design_weaknesses: Many categorical bars and rotated/small labels make individual configurations hard to read.
The PD panel is visually small relative to the placement panel and its y quantity is not fully defined in the caption.
No uncertainty or statistical replication is shown, and color is the only dataset encoding.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair a broad categorical placement panel with a compact privacy-cost panel, while exposing the selection criterion and the exact probe definition in the surrounding text.

figures.label: Figure 5

caption.text: Figure 5. UMAP plots visualize task-relevant (dots) and removed nuisance/sensitive (crosses) features after the first OPL/G-OPL (using RTFM-I3D on MSAD). Colors indicate frame-level labels (normal, abnormal, anomaly types). Removal operates at the feature level, anomalies are detected from the remaining task-relevant features, not from removed components. (a) vs. (c): Both OPL and G-OPL successfully disentangle nuisance/sensitive features (crosses) from task-relevant ones (dots), but G-OPL yields more compact clusters of removed features due to its guidance from facial cues, offering clearer separation of irrelevant information. (b) vs. (d): For task-relevant features, G-OPL preserves more compact and semantically meaningful clusters for human-centric anomalies (e.g., robbery, vandalism), revealing improved disentanglement of anomaly-relevant factors.

color.semantic_mapping: Gray/red identify normal/abnormal; black dot/cross distinguish task-relevant versus removed features; category colors in anomaly-type panels identify the 12 anomaly labels.

figures.data_and_statistics: UMAP projections of retained and removed frame-level features after the first OPL/G-OPL on RTFM-I3D/MSAD. Points are qualitative samples; axes, units, aggregation, sample denominator, and uncertainty are absent.
figures.evidence_relation: Feature-disentanglement mechanism → Figure 5 retained-versus-removed qualitative evidence → Figure 1 removed-feature complement → Figure 6 projection-matrix mechanism → Tables 2–5 utility/privacy metrics. It directly supports separation language but not a numerical separability estimate.
design_strengths: Dot/cross shape redundancy makes the retained-versus-removed distinction explicit.
The binary and anomaly-type views let the same feature operation be checked at two semantic resolutions.
Full-width placement gives the dense legends and four panels more room than the single-column UMAP teaser.
design_weaknesses: Four legends and dense point clouds remain difficult to inspect at paper scale.
No axes, embedding parameters, point count, or quantitative cluster criterion are provided.
The raster has no matching public asset or plotting source; the color map is not grayscale-safe.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a full-width four-panel embedding to separate feature role (shape) from semantic label (color), and accompany it with an explicit statement that removed components are not used for anomaly scoring.

figures.label: Figure 6

caption.text: Figure 6. Visualization of QQ⊤ (G-OPL of RTFM model) from detected (det.) and generated (gen.) faces on ShanghaiTech (ShT) and UCF-Crime (UCF). Central 100×100 regions, where energy concentrates, are shown to better reveal informative subspace patterns. All matrices are log-scaled, globally min-max normalized. Differences reflect dataset- and signal-specific subspace structures, highlighting distinct patterns of sensitive feature disentanglement.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue-white-red intensity encodes normalized entries of QQ⊤; panels vary dataset (ShT/UCF) and face source (detected/generated).

encodings.color: log-scaled globally min-max normalized QQ⊤ energy

figures.data_and_statistics: Four 100×100 central regions of projection matrices are shown as image heatmaps. The caption specifies log scaling and global min-max normalization; no uncertainty, repeated matrices, axes, or numeric color bar is displayed.
figures.evidence_relation: Projection-matrix interpretation → Figure 6 visualizes sensitive directions under detected versus generated guidance → Eqs. (1)–(8) and Algorithm 2 explain QQ⊤ → Figure 5 and SSC/FPD/ArcFace tables provide behavioral checks. The heatmaps are mechanistic evidence, not a quantitative matrix comparison.
design_strengths: Matched 2×2 facets isolate dataset and guidance-source effects.
Central crop and normalization make otherwise dense matrix structure visible in a small panel.
The caption states the transform and crop, preventing a raw-color reading of the pixels.
design_weaknesses: No color bar, matrix coordinate labels, or numeric range prevents exact value recovery.
Red/blue intensity is not grayscale-safe and visually complex pixel texture may invite over-interpretation.
No public image/source asset was found for these four matrices.
figures.reusable_pattern: For learned projection matrices, use a matched dataset-by-signal heatmap grid with explicit normalization/cropping, and pair it with probe metrics that quantify the visual mechanism.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1. Decoupled analysis of OPL and G-OPL with independently varied ranks kOPL and kG-OPL using ShanghaiTech. The table reports AUC (%) on the validation set. Best performance is achieved at kOPL = 4 and kG-OPL = 4.

tables.uncertainty: 未报告均值±SD/SE、区间、误差条、重复次数或显著性检验；表内的 “-”/“NA” 是缺失或不可检测结果，而不是零。
tables.data_and_statistics: Rows are kOPL ∈ {2,4,8,16,32,64,128}; seven numeric columns are kG-OPL values in the same set; cells are validation AUC (%), one decimal place.
tables.evidence_relation: Independent rank grid tests the decoupled OPL/G-OPL mechanism → Table 1 selects kOPL=kG-OPL=4 → Figure 3 rank sensitivity → Appendix Tables 10–12 per-dataset settings.
design_strengths: A compact square grid exposes interaction between the two ranks.
The best cell is bold and the header names both rank axes.
One decimal place is consistent across the matrix.
design_weaknesses: No uncertainty or validation-set size is reported.
The diagonal/cell color has no additional visual cue; a reader must scan all 49 values.
The caption does not explain whether each cell is a single run or an average.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a two-hyperparameter matrix when both rank choices are the decision surface; bold only the selected cell and state the validation protocol.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2. Performance by anomaly type on MSAD. We compare against recent methods (same for Table 3): RTFM (Tian et al., 2021), MGFN (Chen et al., 2023b), UR-DMU (Zhou et al., 2023), EGO (Ding et al., 2025), and IEF-VAD (Jeong et al., 2025). Bold marks the best, underlined the second-best. Our G-OPL/OPL achieves competitive or superior results across anomaly types, highlighting its robustness, especially when paired with strong base models (e.g., RTFM with I3D).

tables.uncertainty: 未报告均值±SD/SE、区间、误差条、重复次数或显著性检验；表内的 “-”/“NA” 是缺失或不可检测结果，而不是零。 IEF-VAD lacks AP for most columns and is shown with “-”.
tables.data_and_statistics: Rows compare five baseline methods, six OPL variants, and two G-OPL/OPL variants; the 12 anomaly categories plus Overall each have AUC/AP subcolumns.
tables.evidence_relation: MSAD anomaly-type comparison in §4.2 → Table 2 main utility claim → Table 4 cross-dataset privacy utility → Appendix Tables 20/22/24/26 exhaustive placement slices.
design_strengths: Two-level grouped header keeps 24 metric columns interpretable.
Baseline/OPL/G-OPL row blocks and bold/underline best/second-best support rapid comparison.
Overall remains adjacent to category metrics.
design_weaknesses: Twenty-five columns are extremely dense at page scale.
Missing AP is represented by dashes without a denominator or applicability explanation in the table body.
No variability estimate makes small method differences look exact.
tables.reusable_pattern: For many-category evaluation, group each category into metric pairs and preserve method-family blocks; define missing values and best/second-best semantics in the caption.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3. Performance by scenario on MSAD. Results on 12 test scenarios (excluding Highway and Park without anomalies) show our method’s strong adaptability and robustness, consistently outperforming or matching top baselines and recent state-of-the-art methods while achieving better balance across scenarios (this table) and anomaly types (Table 2).

tables.uncertainty: 未报告均值±SD/SE、区间、误差条、重复次数或显著性检验；表内的 “-”/“NA” 是缺失或不可检测结果，而不是零。 IEF-VAD has only the reported overall AUC; unavailable scenario AP cells are “-”.
tables.data_and_statistics: Rows match Table 2; 13 scenario groups including Overall each contain AUC/AP, covering the 12 test scenarios described in the caption.
tables.evidence_relation: Table 2 anomaly-wise claim → Table 3 scenario-wise complement → Figure 5 qualitative semantics → Appendix Tables 21/23/25/27 full placement sensitivity.
design_strengths: Anomaly and scenario tables share row ordering, enabling side-by-side reading.
The caption states the exclusion rule for the 12 test scenarios.
Two-level headers expose both scenario and metric.
design_weaknesses: The 27-column span leaves very small type and little whitespace.
The caption claims balance without defining a summary statistic for “balance”.
Unavailable baseline cells and absent uncertainty complicate exact cross-method interpretation.
tables.reusable_pattern: Mirror the anomaly-wise and scenario-wise tables with identical row blocks and header grammar, and explicitly state scenario exclusions.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4. Results on ShanghaiTech, UCF-Crime, CUHK Avenue, and UCSD Ped2. G-OPL/OPL are further evaluated using privacy metrics (SSC↑, ARD↓, FPD↓). † uses RetinaFace embeddings; NA denotes undetectable faces on UCSD Ped2 due to low resolution. Bold highlights performance surpassing the baseline or the best privacy variant. Privacy metrics may underperform on datasets with low resolution or small/occluded faces. We also include ArcFace-based identity retrieval as a classifier-based privacy probe (Arc↓), providing an external reference point for comparison. MGNAD and SPAct are adapted to VAD; TeD-SPAD follows its own setup using MGFN+I3D. This is the first comprehensive privacy analysis for VAD across datasets.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty intervals or repeated-run summaries. “-” means not reported; “NA” means faces were undetectable on Ped2 for the detected-face variant.
tables.data_and_statistics: Four dataset groups each contain AUC, AP, SSC, ARD, FPD, and Arc, with arrow directions in the headers. Twenty method/variant rows include baselines, OPL, G-OPL, and detected-face dagger rows.
tables.evidence_relation: Main utility/privacy claim → Table 4 unified decision surface → Figure 6 mechanism and Tables 5–8 privacy comparisons → Appendix Tables 9/14/17 probes.
design_strengths: Utility, privacy diagnostics, and ArcFace external probe are co-located.
Dataset group headers and directional arrows identify metric roles.
Bold/underline highlight gains while preserving the baseline rows.
design_weaknesses: Twenty-five columns and six metrics per dataset exceed comfortable reading density.
Metrics have different scales and meanings but share one visual table without normalization.
The caption’s “first comprehensive” claim is not itself a measured table field.
tables.reusable_pattern: Put utility and privacy metrics under identical dataset groups, retain an external attacker probe, and use explicit ↑/↓ header directions.

tables.label: Table 5

caption.text: Table 5. Comparison with representative privacy-preserving strategies across datasets, including input-level masking, noise-based differential privacy (Dwork, 2025), compression-based feature bottleneck, and adversarial learning (GRL) (Ganin et al., 2016). Existing methods exhibit clear privacy-utility trade-offs, while our projection-based methods achieve a better balance, with G-OPL consistently providing stronger privacy and higher utility.

tables.uncertainty: 未报告均值±SD/SE、区间、误差条、重复次数或显著性检验；表内的 “-”/“NA” 是缺失或不可检测结果，而不是零。 The “-” entries in privacy columns are not reported values.
tables.data_and_statistics: Rows are Baseline, input masking, differential privacy, feature bottleneck, GRL, OPL, and G-OPL. Dataset column groups report AUC and FPD/ARD combinations across ShT, CUHK, UCSD, and UCF.
tables.evidence_relation: Table 4 broad privacy-utility claim → Table 5 controlled comparison of representative strategies → Table 6 cost normalization and Tables 7–8 attribute scope.
design_strengths: Compact method-by-strategy comparison keeps competing privacy interventions visible.
AUC and leakage/cost fields put the decision trade-off on one surface.
Bold draws attention to the proposed variant without coloring cells.
design_weaknesses: The ten columns are still small in the lower-right placement.
The caption names strategy families but does not state all metric directions.
No run variation or statistical comparison is available.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a compact controlled-baseline table to compare privacy interventions under the same backbone, then expand metrics in a larger primary table.

tables.label: Table 6

caption.text: Table 6. Privacy-efficiency trade-off measured by privacy-per-GFLOP. ΔFPD is the reduction in FPD relative to the baseline. The ratio ΔFPD/ΔGFLOPs indicates privacy gain per additional computational cost (higher is better).

tables.uncertainty: 未报告均值±SD/SE、区间、误差条、重复次数或显著性检验；表内的 “-”/“NA” 是缺失或不可检测结果，而不是零。
tables.data_and_statistics: Rows are baseline, early/mid/late one-layer variants, and two/three G-OPL stacks. Columns jointly report layer count, GFLOPs, delta GFLOPs, AUC, FPD, delta FPD, and the derived privacy gain per GFLOP ratio.
tables.evidence_relation: Privacy-efficiency claim → Table 6 normalizes privacy gain by compute → Figure 4 placement/PD and Table 18 runtime overhead → deployment recommendation.
design_strengths: Cost and privacy gain share a single compact row grammar.
The ratio column makes the decision criterion explicit and is bolded.
Three-decimal ratio precision preserves small cost differences.
design_weaknesses: The ratio is a derived quantity whose denominator and baseline scope are only partly specified.
AUC and FPD have different directions and scales in one row.
No uncertainty or hardware/runtime context is included.
tables.reusable_pattern: Report absolute utility, privacy change, incremental compute, and a clearly defined normalized gain side by side.

tables.label: Table 7

caption.text: Table 7. Attribute-wise anomaly detection performance and privacy leakage on ShanghaiTech. We report AUC as utility and FPD as a measure of privacy leakage for each attribute, where lower FPD indicates stronger suppression.

tables.uncertainty: 未报告均值±SD/SE、区间、误差条、重复次数或显著性检验；表内的 “-”/“NA” 是缺失或不可检测结果，而不是零。
tables.data_and_statistics: Four attribute rows (Face, Gender, Clothing, Gait) compare Base/+G-OPL AUC and Base/+G-OPL FPD; values are percentages/accuracies with one decimal place.
tables.evidence_relation: Multi-attribute generality claim → Table 7 attribute-wise utility/leakage → Table 8 cumulative suppression → Appendix Table 16 VISPR attribute probes.
design_strengths: Paired Base/+G-OPL columns make direction of change easy to inspect.
Small row count keeps attribute breadth readable.
The caption defines AUC as utility and lower FPD as stronger suppression.
design_weaknesses: The table does not state the probe model or attribute-label construction.
One-decimal values and no uncertainty may overstate differences.
Attribute names do not reveal which are face-conditioned versus proxy cues.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use paired Base/variant subcolumns for mechanism generalization, but define the probe and label construction in the caption or nearby setup.

tables.label: Table 8

caption.text: Table 8. Effect of progressively incorporating identity-related cues, including face, gender, clothing, and gait, on anomaly detection performance (AUC) and attribute leakage (FPD).

tables.uncertainty: 未报告均值±SD/SE、区间、误差条、重复次数或显著性检验；表内的 “-”/“NA” 是缺失或不可检测结果，而不是零。
tables.data_and_statistics: Five cumulative settings (Baseline; Face; Face+Gender; Face+Gender+Clothing; Face+Gender+Clothing+Gait) report AUC and FPD.
tables.evidence_relation: Attribute generality → Table 7 isolated attributes → Table 8 cumulative identity-related cue suppression → Appendix Tables 15–16 for data/attribute checks.
design_strengths: The cumulative sequence directly represents a progressive intervention.
AUC and FPD are adjacent, exposing utility/privacy drift.
Only three columns avoid the density of the main results table.
design_weaknesses: No uncertainty, sample sizes, or ordering rationale beyond the caption.
A cumulative sequence conflates added attribute count with semantic importance.
The caption does not specify whether FPD is one joint probe or averaged across attributes.
tables.reusable_pattern: Show cumulative mechanism expansion as ordered rows with utility and leakage adjacent, then support the sequence with isolated-attribute evidence.

tables.label: Table 9

caption.text: Table 9. Face-presence detection (PD/FPD, ↓) across multiple VAD methods on ShanghaiTech and UCF-Crime. All results are obtained using the same linear probe architecture and training protocol.

tables.uncertainty: 未报告均值±SD/SE、区间、误差条、重复次数或显著性检验；表内的 “-”/“NA” 是缺失或不可检测结果，而不是零。
tables.data_and_statistics: Six baseline/+G-OPL pairs (RTFM, MGFN, SPAct, TeD-SPAD, EGO, TEVAD) report face-presence probe values for ShanghaiTech and UCF-Crime.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix probe generality → Table 9 cross-method PD/FPD evidence → main Table 4 privacy metrics and Figure 4(b) decay curve.
design_strengths: Alternating method/+G-OPL pairs make suppression deltas obvious.
Identical linear-probe protocol is stated in the caption.
A three-column layout is easy to scan.
design_weaknesses: The header says PD/FPD but does not show separate PD versus FPD columns.
No baseline AUC or probe uncertainty accompanies leakage values.
Pair rows rely on visual adjacency rather than an explicit delta column.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use adjacent baseline/variant rows for a cross-method privacy probe, with a caption that fixes the probe protocol.

tables.label: Table 10

caption.text: Table 10. Optimal hyperparameters for RTFM and MGFN across all datasets. † indicates configurations using detected faces. G-OPL and OPL denote the presence of the respective projection layers; λorth and λface are the weights for orthogonality and face alignment losses, respectively. Batch size, training epochs, and resulting AUC and AP scores are also reported.

tables.uncertainty: 未报告均值±SD/SE、区间、误差条、重复次数或显著性检验；表内的 “-”/“NA” 是缺失或不可检测结果，而不是零。
tables.data_and_statistics: Eight dataset/configuration rows report two grouped model blocks (RTFM and MGFN), each with G-OPL, OPL, λorth, λface, batch size, max epoch, AUC, and AP; dagger marks detected-face settings.
tables.evidence_relation: Reproduction setup → Table 10 binds layer counts, loss weights, training budget, and resulting metrics → Figure 3/4 ablations and Appendix Tables 11–13.
design_strengths: Hyperparameters and outcomes are bound in the same row.
RTFM/MGFN groups make backbone-specific settings explicit.
The dagger and loss-weight definitions reduce ambiguity.
design_weaknesses: Seventeen columns are too wide for comfortable inspection.
Different datasets use different training budgets, making direct outcome comparison nontrivial.
No random seeds, hardware, or run aggregation are reported.
tables.reusable_pattern: Bind configuration knobs and resulting metrics in one grouped appendix table, while documenting all omitted reproducibility conditions elsewhere.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: 摘要 Figure 1 先用 removed-feature UMAP 提出 OPL/G-OPL 的互补机制，Figure 2 给出可插入主干的接口与损失流，Figure 3–4 选择 rank/权重/层位置，Figure 5–6 将特征分离与 QQ⊤ 子空间结构可视化；Table 2–8 随后把主比较、隐私诊断、属性范围和成本固定成决策面，Tables 9–29 在附录展开 probe、超参和 placement 搜索。
cross_object_system.caption_system: Figure caption 从短标题（Figure 3）到长型自包含机制说明（Figures 2、5、6）不完全一致；结果 captions 通常同时定义方向、缩写和主发现，但 Figure 3 对设置与编码说明不足。Table captions 基本沿用“设置→指标/编码→结论”的顺序，且大量附录表只提供标题和数据范围。
cross_object_system.table_header_system: 主结果表以方法为 stub、数据集/异常类别/场景为一级分组、AUC/AP 或隐私指标为二级分组；附录 placement 表复用 MSAD anomaly/scenario 头部，跨数据集表复用 dataset×AUC/AP。箭头明确部分指标方向，缺失值用 “-” 或 “NA”。
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 2 的 OPL/G-OPL 接口和投影损失由 Figure 3 的超参曲线、Figure 4 的 placement/PD 柱图、Tables 1/11/12/19 的选择网格与 Tables 20–29 的完整配置矩阵逐层验证；Tables 2–8 和 Figures 1/5/6 将这些设计选择连接到效用、隐私和机制主张。
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: 正文 Figure 2 明确指向 Appendix H/I/M；正文 Figure 4 和 Tables 2–8 的结论分别由 Tables 9–19 的探针/设置/失败分析与 Tables 20–29 的全量 placement 切片支撑。附录包含 Algorithms 1–2（p.19），它们是伪代码而非 Figure/Table，不进入数组但闭合 Figure 2 的算法接口。
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: PDF text objects 的 Nimbus Roman No9 L 与 Computer Modern math 在标题、caption、表格中一致；图内 raster 字体只能从 rendered/source asset 估计，通常是 DejaVu Sans，字号和图例密度在缩小到论文栏宽后不一致。
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Figure 2 的浅蓝/深蓝/红/紫有方法语义，Figure 3–4 的蓝红/彩色数据集语义局部稳定，UMAP 和 heatmap 使用各自独立的类别/发散色；跨图没有固定的同一类别颜色映射，灰度读者需依赖 panel、shape、线型或表头。

most_reusable_patterns: 用 Figure 2 的左到右主干加独立训练信号箭头表达可插拔模块，并在 caption 定义全部颜色和损失。
把 anomaly-wise 与 scenario-wise 表按相同方法块和 AUC/AP 二级表头成对组织。
用 Figure 5 的 shape（保留/移除）+ color（任务标签）冗余编码特征角色，再用 probe 表把定性分离连接到可量化隐私。
用 rank/regularizer 网格、placement 小倍图和 cross-dataset appendix matrix 构成从选择到迁移的证据链。
highest_value_objects: Figure 2：方法接口、三类 loss 和可插入位置在一个视觉对象中闭合。
Table 4：四数据集上的 AUC/AP、SSC/ARD/FPD 和 ArcFace 形成统一 utility/privacy decision surface。
Figure 5：直接呈现 retained 与 removed feature 的角色分离，是机制主张最易复核的定性证据。
Figure 4 + Tables 6/9：将 placement、privacy decay 和计算成本连接起来。
failure_patterns: Figure 3、宽表和附录 placement matrices 信息密度过高，图例/表头在论文缩放下难以读取。
